items.item: The developed frame and temples implement the written selection and preserve the specification's dimensions, component arrangement, controls and operating-state definitions.
Material assignments and selected colour codes on the application board agree with the anatomy and wearing/operation views, allowing ordinary lighting and perspective variation.
The case develops the selected case decisions and accommodates the same folded glasses dimensions and right-temple contact locations recorded in the specification and anatomy.
Open charging, closed storage and the empty inset retain the same case construction, key, tips, lens-clear supports, access, exterior indicator and material palette.
Docked glasses are fully folded with the slider closed; charging is steady amber, and the externally visible stored/idle case indicator is off.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Show a complete adult eyewear concept with two transparent lenses without displays, a bridge, two folding temples, paired nose and ear contact regions, integrated components and identifiable physical controls. Form and hinge design may vary. Missing eyewear parts, display lenses, visibly intersecting folded temples or rigid modules crossing moving hinges fail; actual comfort is not established by a rendering.

Record 42 g as the maximum design target. Delivered drawings cannot establish measured mass, and the supplied facts explicitly leave mass unmeasured; this diagnostic does not require a weighing result or fail an image for apparent weight.

Interpret the concept as deliberate image capture followed by a user-initiated spoken question with paired-phone assistance. This input defines the interaction context without requiring an additional phone interface deliverable or proof of functioning electronics.

Each exploration board must name an alternative and show its complete glasses both open and folded with its own matching case. The three alternatives must differ recognisably in product design decisions such as frame, temples or case construction; merely changing names or recolouring the same concept is insufficient. Alternatives may legitimately differ from the subsequently selected design.

The selection record must choose exactly one of the three named explorations and state the frame, temple and case decisions carried forward. The presentation's first page must identify that same choice. The specification must develop those decisions without introducing an unexplained alternative. The records must establish alternatives followed by selection; no particular rationale format is required. Conflicting selections, an unnamed choice or missing carried-forward decisions fail.

Read actual chosen dimensions, not only allowable maxima: front width 140–150 mm; each hinge-axis-to-tip centreline length 135–150 mm; largest temple height/thickness at most 18/12 mm; folded envelope at most 150×60×48 mm; closed case at most 170×85×65 mm; and a defined usable cavity allowing at least 2 mm on all six sides except marked support/contact interfaces. Record both right-temple pad-centre distances within 60 mm, with P+ nearer the hinge and their difference 6 mm. Choices within the ranges are allowed; absent selected values or internally incompatible records fail.

Read the dimension records on the anatomy and both case boards and compare them with the specification. Selected open and folded values and both pad-centre positions must repeat without numerical drift. Show the stated front-width and temple-length ranges, section and envelope limits, chosen cavity dimensions and at least 2 mm clearance on each of six sides, with any support/contact exceptions explicitly marked. Dimensions may be placed in insets or record panels; an outer case dimension alone does not demonstrate cavity fit. Any out-of-range selection, missing required repeated record or incompatible clearance fails.

The sheet must record exactly one each of C01 28×8×5, B01 30×7×4, B02 30×7×4, S01 16×5×3, S02 16×5×3, K01 8×8×6, M01 4×3×2, I01 3×2×1, CB01 45×25×6, CC01 20×15×4 and U01 12×5×7 mm in local X/Y/Z order, plus schematic connections. C01 may occupy either temple; B01/S01 belong in the left temple and B02/S02 in the right, with speakers near ears; K01 belongs at an outer front corner, M01 in the frame or forward temple, I01 on the front beside K01, CB01/CC01 in the case and U01 at its wall. Preserve original envelopes under rotation, identify local orientations, and state at least 1 mm separation and enclosure with functional-opening exceptions. Missing modules, quantities, connections, incorrect dimensions or placement outside permitted regions fail.

The anatomy must contain front, top and right orthographic views, all eight labelled glasses envelopes with recorded dimensions and local axes, and schematic wiring matching the specification. The charging board must label all three case envelopes with matching dimensions. Placement and sections must support 1 mm minimum envelope separation and enclosure except functional openings; enclosed batteries, outward/downward speaker openings near open ear canals, an outward microphone opening away from skin and hinges, and an exposed case-wall U01 mouth must be coherent. Show K01's 4 mm aperture and an outward front I01 centre within 12 mm. The anatomy's B01 explosion must visibly separate the accessible cover and detachable connection and include a removal arrow beside the required wording. Symbolic module blocks are allowed; conflicting records or labels without credible integration fail.

Both documents must identify all three states and preserve their distinctions: READY means exposed camera, front light off and no active capture; CAPTURE means deliberate button operation, exposed camera and steady white front light; PRIVACY means an opaque slider covering the whole aperture, a visible position mark, front light off and camera/microphone capture inhibited even when the button is pressed. Text, diagrams or a state table may communicate the behaviour. Missing states, software-only privacy or contradictory light/capture behaviour fail.

Read W1/READY and W2/PRIVACY on the assigned boards and CAPTURE on the operation board. W1 must show an adult standing in a quiet urban pause, open glasses in a three-quarter upper-body view, an exposed camera with light off and an inset resolving silicone nose/ear contacts. CAPTURE must show an exposed camera, steady white front indicator and a reachable button whose finger path leaves the aperture and lenses clear. W2 must show an adult seated at a desk wearing the glasses, a hand near the button, complete opaque camera coverage, visible slider mark, unlit externally visible indicator and evidence that a press cannot activate camera or microphone capture. People and clothing may vary; product geometry and state behaviour must match the sources.

The open charging board must seat the selected fully folded glasses with the opaque slider closed, a visible locating key, lens-clear frame/temple supports and finger access. Its mating section must show two flush right-temple underside pads, 2 mm diameter and 6 mm centre spacing, mating to two 1.2 mm tips of matching spacing and polarity with parallel contact faces. Both selected centre distances must be labelled within 60 mm of the right hinge, with P+ nearer it. Show steady amber on a separate case indicator only after seating and contact; unplugged charging uses the internal case battery. The closed stored case must contain the same assembly and show its externally visible indicator off. Its empty open-case inset must retain the same key, tips, supports and access. Construction details may vary from other designers' solutions, but inconsistency between these boards fails.

The material board must assign named materials, finishes and selected colour codes to the glasses and case: satin TR90 frame/temple shells, anodised aluminium hinges and smooth silicone nose/ear contacts. Case materials and palette are designer choices, but their assignments must be explicit. Mark compliant skin-contact zones with rounded transitions and separation from sharp edges, open ports and charging pads. The anatomy glasses and stored case must carry LUMA on the objects themselves, and their surfaces must agree with the material board. Unmapped swatches, substituted required materials or title-only branding fail.

The component/state specification must record the contact-material assignments. The presentation must name the required shell, hinge and contact materials and finishes and repeat the selected colour codes shown on the material application board. Additional case materials are allowed as selected design choices. Missing contact materials, contradictory required assignments or inconsistent presentation colour codes fail.

Review the complete 12-second video for the ordered progression READY, CAPTURE, PRIVACY, fully folded docking and closed-case stored/idle. READY exposes the camera with its light off; deliberate CAPTURE uses a reachable control without obstructing the camera or pressing lenses and shows steady white front light; PRIVACY fully covers the camera with an opaque marked slider, turns the light off and communicates camera/microphone inhibition. Dock only with the slider closed, using the same keyed seat, parallel matching contacts and lens-clear frame/temple supports. The separate case indicator becomes steady amber after mating and is visibly off on the closed stored case. Product dimensions, components, material assignments and colours must agree with the supplied source boards and specification. Editing and camera motion may vary; omitted or reordered states, changing product geometry, premature charging or contradictory privacy behaviour fail.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation must contain at least eight pages and visibly reuse recognisable material from every listed source role, including the written selection and component/state specification. It must include the LUMA-marked glasses and case views. Cropping, scaling and re-layout are allowed if the reused design and essential labels remain identifiable; a source name, link or generic summary alone is insufficient reuse. Too few pages, an omitted source or substituted conflicting artwork fails.

The developed frame and temples implement the written selection and preserve the specification's dimensions, component arrangement, controls and operating-state definitions. Material assignments and selected colour codes on the application board agree with the anatomy and wearing/operation views, allowing ordinary lighting and perspective variation.

The case develops the selected case decisions and accommodates the same folded glasses dimensions and right-temple contact locations recorded in the specification and anatomy. Open charging, closed storage and the empty inset retain the same case construction, key, tips, lens-clear supports, access, exterior indicator and material palette. Docked glasses are fully folded with the slider closed; charging is steady amber, and the externally visible stored/idle case indicator is off.
